source.title: Theta-burst transcranial magnetic stimulation to the prefrontal or parietal cortex does not impair metacognitive visual awareness

confidence_rationale: Weakens ARC-116 only indirectly: it removes the best-known causal demonstration that a metacognitive readout can be degraded independently of first-order performance, by failing to replicate Rounis et al. 2010 in two experiments (between- and within-subjects, with an active control site). It does not show collapse -- a null on one stimulation target is not evidence that readout and generation are one computation -- so confidence in the weakening is modest.
failure_signatures: No cTBS-induced metacognitive impairment was found after DLPFC or posterior parietal stimulation in a between-subjects design, nor after DLPFC in a rigorous within-subjects design.

Including data unsuitable for signal detection analysis reproduced a significant but invalid metacognitive impairment, showing how a spurious readout/generation dissociation can be manufactured by analysis choices -- a direct hazard for any REE falsifier using a meta-d'-style readout measure.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In two experiments, continuous theta-burst TMS to DLPFC (and, in one, posterior parietal cortex) produced no metacognitive impairment relative to an active control site; a significant but invalid impairment appeared only when data unsuitable for SDT analysis were included.
mapping.ree_translation: The empirical case that stage 2 (readout) can be selectively degraded while stage 1 (generation) is spared is weaker than the TMS literature once suggested. ARC-116's separation therefore leans more on existence arguments (readout without reconstruction, reconstruction without generation) than on clean causal dissociations -- which is exactly why the claim's own falsifier (a built dissociation under degradation) matters.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A null at one cortical site under one stimulation protocol does not show that readout and generation are the same computation; it shows this manipulation does not separate them. The paper addresses stage 1 vs 2, not stage 2 vs 3.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adults, visual discrimination with visibility/confidence ratings; cTBS to DLPFC or PPC vs active control site; between- and within-subjects designs; SDT analysis with strict exclusion.

confidence_components.notes: Careful replication, open access. The SDT-exclusion point is the most transferable lesson for REE instrument design.
